title: MutationObserver
learningObjectives: Explain mutationobserver and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: MutationObserver watches DOM changes such as child additions, attribute changes, and text updates. observe() configures the target and options; disconnect() stops observation; takeRecords() retrieves queued records.
understand.whyItMatters: It can integrate with DOM regions modified by other code, but observing too broadly can create unnecessary work or feedback loops. Prefer direct application events when you control the mutation source.
understand.analogy: A MutationObserver is a change log watcher for a selected part of the DOM tree.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The observer reports matching DOM mutations under the selected target.

examples.explanation: The observer reports matching DOM mutations under the selected target.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Observe a list for newly added children and update a count. Disconnect the observer when the component is removed.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which method stops a MutationObserver from watching its target?
questions.explanation: disconnect stops the observer from receiving further mutation records.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
